builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models
summary: The method replaces round-to-nearest activation quantization in low-bit world models used by sampling-based planners with stochastic rounding whose dither is shared across candidates and redrawn each planner iteration, requiring no retraining or calibration. It costs at most 2.3% added latency and implementation complexity in the quantized forward pass, while the headline speedup does not exceed BF16 with pre-converted weights, so gains depend on having integer kernels that beat a BF16 baseline. Failure modes include any planner or model variant where error persists across iterations or is not shared across candidates (fixed dither reintroduces the drift), and results are validated mainly on TD-MPC2, DINO-WM, and Meta-World, so transfer to other stacks is unverified.
rationale: The reader can apply this training-free to quantized world models, but the benefit only materializes if they run sampling-based planning with low-bit models on hardware where integer inference beats BF16, so workload-specific validation is required before adoption.
technique: Shared-dither stochastic rounding for low-bit world models

claims.statement: The method replaces round-to-nearest activation quantization in low-bit world models used by sampling-based planners with stochastic rounding whose dither is shared across candidates and redrawn each planner iteration, requiring no retraining or calibration. It costs at most 2.3% added latency and implementation complexity in the quantized forward pass, while the headline speedup does not exceed BF16 with pre-converted weights, so gains depend on having integer kernels that beat a BF16 baseline. Failure modes include any planner or model variant where error persists across iterations or is not shared across candidates (fixed dither reintroduces the drift), and results are validated mainly on TD-MPC2, DINO-WM, and Meta-World, so transfer to other stacks is unverified.

W8A4 integer TD-MPC2 world model runs planning rollouts 1.9-3.3x and the whole planning step 1.3-1.5x faster than FP32 on an Ampere GPU, though not faster than BF16 with pre-converted weights; shared dither adds at most 2.3% latency.
